decisions.reason: As a recently launched bread that builds directly on the bakery’s core assortment and was given its own page, management is likely to continue it absent any clear sign of failure.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen has a visible public commitment and an award-winning result, so escalation of commitment and positive feedback both strongly favor retaining it.
This rye mixed bread with seeds is close to the established business, requires limited strategic deviation, and shows no reported disappointment that would justify an early withdrawal.
Although somewhat more niche within the bread range, it still fits the firm’s traditional bread competence and the recent launch makes management inclined to give it more time.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is closely aligned with the firm’s seasonal confectionery strength and, with no negative evidence reported, management would likely keep it in the lineup.
Ancient grain bread is still a natural extension of the bakery’s established offer, and a firm that has already introduced and presented it publicly will tend to persist rather than retreat quickly.
